prompt:
You are a grounded brand-outreach assistant for our team. Use only the evidence passages below.
Never use outside knowledge. Return valid JSON only.

Separate three things:
1. OBSERVED FACTS - things a passage actually states about this company. Each fact is a claim with an id (C1, C2, ...),
   the passage id(s) that support it, and an exact quote copied word-for-word from that passage.
2. UNKNOWNS - things the evidence does not tell us (put them in "unknowns"). A channel, program or audience that does
   not appear in these passages is UNKNOWN. It is never a weakness, never a "gap", and never a reason for outreach.
3. PROPOSALS - collaboration ideas from our team. Proposals are not facts, but each must build on a positively supported
   fact (an existing campaign, partnership, product, community, value or theme) and cite that premise.

Rules:
- Put a claim marker like {C1} (curly braces) right after every factual statement in every field, including the
  email and Instagram idea. Do not write citation numbers yourself; markers are converted to citations later.
- A claim's "quote" must be copied character-for-character from the cited passage: 5 to 25 consecutive words, no
  paraphrasing, no joining of separate sentences. If you cannot find such a quote, drop the claim and every sentence
  that depends on it.
- Audience and strategy sentences are factual: each needs a marker. If no passage states the audience, write
  INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE instead of guessing.
- Pitch lines (email subject, hook, concept) should describe the proposed post ("A carousel featuring ...",
  "Collaborate on ..."). Any statement in them about what the company already does needs a marker.
- Respect passage types. "proposed_or_mock_work" and "author_recommendation" passages describe ideas, not things the
  company did: never state them as company activity. "provider_reported_result" passages are claims by a vendor or
  agency: attribute them ("X reports that ..."). "creator_or_influencer_audience_data" describes creators' followers,
  not the company's customers. "vendor_generated_profile_or_analytics" passages are a tool vendor's estimates
  (e.g. inferred age ranges): attribute them and never present them as the company's own data.
  "forward_looking_statement" passages describe plans or intentions, not completed activity.
- Mind time: if a passage describes past activity, do not present it as current.
- "marketing_gaps" may only contain a weakness that a passage positively states. Usually it is [].
- Never promise results. Describe benefits as goals or possibilities ("could", "aims to"), not guaranteed outcomes.
- Decision: write "draft" when at least one concrete, evidence-supported collaboration opportunity exists. Otherwise write
  "abstain", give an abstain_reason, set pitch fields to INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE and leave collaboration_opportunities empty.
- The email is from our team to the company, proposing one collaborative Instagram post. The pitch, the post idea and
  every collaboration opportunity are for Instagram only (no TikTok, YouTube, podcasts or other channels).
- When a sentence uses a vendor, agency or analytics passage, name that source in the sentence itself
  ("According to AdLibrary, ...", "Attentive reports that ...").
- Each "unknowns" item names one specific thing the passages do not tell us (e.g. "Whether X runs a creator program").
  Never write placeholder text such as "what the evidence does not show".

Required JSON:
{
  "decision": "draft" or "abstain",
  "abstain_reason": "string or empty",
  "claims": [{"id": "C1", "kind": "fact | provider_reported | premise", "statement": "string",
              "passage_ids": ["P1"], "quote": "exact words from the passage"}],
  "brand_summary": "Full sentences, each followed by its marker, e.g. "X makes ... {C1}." Never only markers. Or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "likely_target_audience": "A full sentence followed by its marker, or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "current_marketing_strategy": ["text with markers"],
  "unknowns": ["one specific open question, e.g. Whether the company works with creators"],
  "marketing_gaps": [],
  "collaboration_opportunities": ["proposal that builds on a cited fact {C2}"],
  "instagram_post_idea": {"hook": "string", "concept": "string", "why_it_fits": "string"},
  "email_subject": "string",
  "email_body": "string"
}

Company: SKIMS (company_id skims; category: shapewear and clothing)
Official domains: skims.com
Recipient: the marketing team
Packet status: ok

Evidence passages:
[P1] source: https://skims.com/pages/about | document: official_domain | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Seasonal Prints holiday shop Holiday Shop Back with even more festive prints, seasonal shades, and new, limited-edition styles Holiday Shop"

[P2] source: https://skims.com/pages/about | document: official_domain | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Tops Search closed Search closed main imagemain image # SKIMS is a solutions-oriented brand creating the next generation of underwear, loungewear and"

[P3] source: https://www.latterly.org/skims-marketing-strategy/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: actual_activity | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"The NBA partnership supports men’s expansion with athlete storytelling, broadcast integrations, and retail displays that anchor comfort and everyday performance credibly. * Team USA loungewear collaborations elevated global visibility and comfort positioning, associating SKIMS with disciplined performance and travel needs across major events. * The Fendi x SKIMS capsule demonstrated luxury collaboration rigor, driving rapid sellouts and reinforcing the brand’s ability to command premium pricing internationally. * The Swarovski collaboration introduced embellished intimates and occasionwear, creating gifting moments that strengthened holiday merchandising and average order value."

[P4] source: https://www.latterly.org/skims-marketing-strategy/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: actual_activity | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Product naming, color stories, and fabric tags allow merchandising teams to build cohesive landing pages around campaigns. Content showcases transformation before-and-after visuals and movement tests, which underline functional outcomes. Clear benefits reduce friction, lifting add-to-cart from social click-throughs and paid traffic alike. SKIMS pairs evergreen continuity with scarcity moments that energize demand and accelerate list growth. Collaborations and event-driven capsules introduce new audiences without straying from the comfort-performance core. These launches also generate earned media that compounds paid efficiency across the funnel."

[P5] source: https://www.latterly.org/skims-marketing-strategy/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Influencer Partnerships and Community Engagement SKIMS scales influence through a portfolio approach that mixes celebrity, athlete, and community voices. High-visibility ambassadors create cultural moments, while micro-creators deliver detailed fit education at scale. This balance keeps the brand aspirational and grounded in real-world results. Major campaigns feature entertainers and athletes who extend reach beyond traditional fashion audiences. The men’s launch starred Neymar Jr, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, and Nick Bosa, signaling performance credibility."

[P6] source: https://www.enrichlabs.ai/case-study/skims-marketing-strategy | document: third_party_confirmed | type: provider_reported_result | flags: vendor_generated_profile_or_analytics | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"How Does SKIMS Leverage Social Media for Marketing? ### A Multi-Channel Strategy SKIMS capitalizes on influencer collaborations, inclusivity, timely content, and community engagement to boost brand awareness and sales. Celebrity partnerships, notably Kim Kardashian, generate initial buzz. Micro-influencers with diverse backgrounds produce authentic, relatable content, showcasing products in real-life contexts. This approach increases trust and engagement Source: Click Analytic. To deepen your social media strategy, explore social-listening complete guide."

[P7] source: https://www.enrichlabs.ai/case-study/skims-marketing-strategy | document: third_party_confirmed | type: provider_reported_result | flags: vendor_generated_profile_or_analytics | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Strategic Timing and Community Building SKIMS schedules product launches and collaborations during cultural moments—Fendi, Lana Del Ray, or limited-edition drops—to generate FOMO. Kim Kardashian’s massive social media presence (over 364 million followers on Instagram) amplifies the message. The brand actively engages followers through comments and feedback, cultivating a loyal, authentic community. Their social media audience has grown by roughly 10% every six months, reaching over 7 million followers [Sources: Click Analytic; Keyhole]. Maximize your reach with social media brand advocacy."

[P8] source: https://www.enrichlabs.ai/case-study/skims-marketing-strategy | document: third_party_confirmed | type: provider_reported_result | flags: vendor_generated_profile_or_analytics | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Mastery of Social Media SKIMS uses TikTok and Instagram to create a community. Hashtags like #skimshaul encourage user participation. The brand partners with nano and micro-influencers to reach different segments, tailoring content to trending topics and seasons."

[P9] source: https://www.kolsquare.com/en/blog/skims-the-marketing-strategy-behind-kim-kardashians-shapewear-success | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | flags: creator_or_influencer_audience_data | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Influencer marketing at SKIMS: Collaborations and influencer strategy deep-dive ### SKIMS influencer strategy on Instagram In the last 12 months, 7.8k creators mentioned SKIMS in 29.4k posts. The engagement rate for creator content on Instagram is 3.3%, and the potential audience size is 4.8 billion."

[P10] source: https://www.kolsquare.com/en/blog/skims-the-marketing-strategy-behind-kim-kardashians-shapewear-success | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Collaborations with purpose SKIMS’ strategic influencer partnerships align with its values and resonate with its audience. When looking for influencers, focus on influencers and partners who authentically represent your brand and values, creating a meaningful connection with your target demographic. * Don’t be afraid to stand out Kim knows the power of standing out from the crowd. The brand leverages eye-catching visuals and provocative imagery, leading to viral content and engagement. * Adapt to evolving trends SKIMS is no longer just shapewear. At the onset of the pandemic, SKIMS was quick to introduce loungewear to meet customer’s new desire for comfort."
